newsitem.title: UK: Thai baht claws back ground vs dollar in London.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht claws back ground vs dollar in London.

text.p: The Thai baht clawed back ground against the dollar in offshore trading on Friday after Thailand's new finance minister Thanong Bidaya said he will announce his policies in the coming days.

While the baht has reversed the losses which saw it set a 98-month low Thursday, traders are expecting it to come under renewed pressure in the weeks ahead as speculators test the new finance minister's resolve to prevent a devaluation.
"The whole thing is far from over and it is very dangerous the way they are allowing the offshore market to do its own thing," said a dealer in London.
"They will hold out as long as possible against the speculators but it's all a question of the economic costs of such a policy."
The baht was quoted at 23.800/000 per dollar in London at 1420 GMT from 26.000/100 late in the domestic market and its 26.80 low Thursday. The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.79.

Analysts said the success with which the government staves off any devaluation will depend on the outlook for Thai growth. Expectations the growth rate will fall below six percent, from 6.7 percent in 1996, have been one of the key triggers for the recent run on the baht. -- Swaha Pattanaik, London newsroom, +44 171 542 6284
